title: Nicaea II’s constant teaching: Christ’s and the saints’ images are to be adored—and doubters are anathematized
source_text: IV. Quod spectat secundum Concilium Nicenum, quod in Schola Romana Universale septimum appellatur, constans & manifesta illius doctrina est, adorandas esse Christi & sanctorum imagines. Nam in epistola hujus Concilii ad Constantinum & Irenem circa finem haec verba habentur. His ita se habentibus in confesso & sine ulla dubitatione credimus, acceptam & placitam coram Deo esse venerandarum imaginum depictionem, & earum quae dispensationem Domini Nostri Jesu Christi exprimunt, & Virginis quoque Deiparae intemeratae, quinetiam gloriosorum Angelorum, & omnium Sanctorum, has quoque adorandas & salutandas putamus. Qui vero ita non est animatus, sed circa Venerandarum imaginum adorationem laborat & dubitat, eum anathematizat sancta & veneranda nostra Synodus. Tom. 3. Conc. Edit. Coloniensis Anni 1606. pag. 391. litt. A.
pass_a_gloss: As for the second Nicene Council, which in the Roman School is called the seventh Universal, its constant and manifest doctrine is that the images of Christ and of the saints are to be adored. For in the epistle of this Council to Constantine and Irene near the end these words are had. Things being thus confessed, and without any doubt we believe that the depiction of venerable images is accepted and pleasing before God, and of those which express the dispensation of Our Lord Jesus Christ, and also of the undefiled Virgin Mother of God, and even of the glorious Angels, and of all the Saints; these also we think are to be adored and saluted. But him who is not so minded, but labors and doubts about the adoration of venerable images, our holy and venerable Synod anathematizes. Tom. 3. Conc. Edit. Coloniensis of the year 1606, p. 391, letter A.
pass_b_english: Nicaea II (Rome’s ‘seventh’) steadily teaches that Christ’s and the saints’ images are to be adored and saluted.
Whoever hesitates about that adoration is anathematized.

choices.why: Council’s own claim that depiction and adoration of images please God.
